newsitem.title: CROATIA: Raiffeisen Croatia plans to triple business in '97.
newsitem.headline: Raiffeisen Croatia plans to triple business in '97.

text.p: The Croatian subsidiary of Austria's Raiffeisen Zentralbank Osterreich AG, the first foreign bank to have opened in the former Yugoslav republic, said on Friday it planned to triple its business in Croatia next year.
"Our aim is to reach a trade portfolio of 250 million German marks in 1997," member of the bank's board Zdenko Adrovic told an international investment conference.
He said this year's portfolio was estimated at around 80 million marks after the bank doubled its capital. Its depositor base had increased 600 percent.
"We are planning to open branch offices throughout Croatia, starting with Rijeka," Adrovic said, adding that its expansion in retails would be focused on the coastal regions.
He said the bank was preparing to offer favourable car, housing and multi-purpose loans to Croatian citizens. At the moment it only supports companies.
"Our aim is to establish ourselves as a serious player," he added. -- Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
